figures.caption: Figure 1: Patient-level respiratory-event burden in iSLEEPS, measured as the fraction of 30-s epochs containing the onset of a scored respiratory event. The dashed line denotes the cohort median of 13%.
Table 1 Datasets used in the study and their roles in the evaluation.

Figure 2: The two-stream, multi-task model. The neural stream combines 188 engineered descriptors with the embedding of a LaBraM encoder adapted to sleep from EEG and EOG and integrated by cross-fitting and alignment; the cardiorespiratory stream is a convolutional encoder over eight raw channels. The streams are fused and read by a bidirectional LSTM over a 20-epoch window, which feeds a staging head and a respiratory head; the respiratory head also reads the cardiorespiratory embedding directly, and the AHI is computed from the respiratory scores over decoded sleep.

Table 3 Training configuration of the final MM-Net, shared across all folds and cohorts. The frozen-encoder configuration uses the same settings with a frozen encoder, concatenation and square-root class weights. Each reimplemented baseline is trained at its own published settings.

Table 4 Patient-independent sleep-staging comparison on iSLEEPS. Values are mean ± SD where fold-level results are available. † denotes reimplemented models, ‡ a literature-reported result under its original protocol, and ∗ models ported from released code. Bold indicates the best result among models evaluated under our protocol.

Figure 3: An illustrative held-out night (patient SN90, three-seed MM-Net, staging accuracy 0.83). (A) Predicted and reference hypnograms, REM highlighted. (B) EEG spectrogram, C4 derivation, 0–25Hz. (C) Per-epoch stage-probability ribbon; the black line is the maximum posterior.
Figure 4: Row-normalized confusion matrix for MM-Net (three-seed, pooled ten-fold test epochs, hidden-Markov operating point). Errors concentrate on N1, which is absorbed into Wake and N2.

Table 6 From the frozen-encoder configuration to MM-Net on iSLEEPS, one change per row (upper block), and the complete model (lower block); same ten folds and three seeds throughout. 𝑝: Wilcoxon on fold means against the row marked ref.

Figure 5: Per-fold staging accuracy of MM-Net with the sleep-adapted encoder, relative to the frozen-encoder reference (three-seed, ten patient-independent folds). The training embeddings are cross-fitted in both cases; aligning them to the deployed encoder turns an inconsistent effect into a gain in eight folds of ten.
Figure 6: t-SNE [55] of 4000 epochs from the ten held-out patients of one fold, colored by scored stage. Left: frozen LaBraM. Right: the sleep-adapted, aligned EEG/EOG encoder used in MM-Net.

Table 7 Respiratory-event detection on iSLEEPS. (A) Comparison with classical and raw-signal baselines on the same folds (§single seed) and (B) MM-Net AUC by respiratory-event type. Bold denotes the best value in each comparison.

Figure 7: Respiratory-event detection by MM-Net (three-seed), pooled over the ten patient-independent test folds. (a) ROC curve. (b) Precision–recall; the dashed line is the 0.160 event prevalence, the no-skill floor.

Table 8 Joint multi-task training against matched single-task models with the same architecture, folds, seeds, training budget and decoding. MM-Net staging: three-seed ensemble; respiratory AUC and AP: mean over seeds. 𝑝: Wilcoxon on the ten fold means, or on patients for the severe-apnea group and the per-patient accuracy. The single-task AHI combines the stages of the staging-only model with the scores of the respiratory-only model.

Figure 8: MM-Net AHI estimate against the annotated AHI. Left: iSLEEPS, ten-fold test patients. Right: ISRUC-I, MMNet trained on iSLEEPS only and applied without retraining (Section 5.10). Shading marks the AASM severity bands; the dashed line is identity.

Table 13 Trained and tested on ISRUC-Sleep. ISRUC-I: ten subject-independent folds (80/10/10 subjects), three seeds; baselines retrained on the same folds with three seeds (accuracy mean ± SD over folds). MM-Net is ahead of every baseline in nine or ten folds of ten (Wilcoxon, Holm 𝑝 = 0.018). ISRUC-II+III: six folds keeping both nights of a subject together. Encoder alone: sleep-adapted EEG/EOG LaBraM, one epoch, no temporal model. Frozen-encoder configuration: class weights, concatenation, seven cardiorespiratory channels. AHI is reported for ISRUC-I, whose 100 patients span the severity range.
